capabilities: Draws a folder's cards and their links as a navigable structure
Opens PDFs, images and Markdown in draggable, resizable reader windows
Writes or deletes [[links]] by dragging lines between cards
Hides card content for recall and reveals it on click
Creates cards from a read-and-jot panel beside the page
disambiguation: Not a vault-wide encryption or sync tool; a "crystal" is a subfolder of cards, and the plugin works on one card folder at a time.
extras: Interface labels are Chinese only; localisation is not done. The optional CrystalFloat companion (~107 MB) is needed for OS-level floating windows. Manual boxes are stored in a dot-prefixed .crystal-boxes.json per crystal, which sync channels that skip dot files will not carry.
intentEvidence: It is not a better graph. It is a different starting point.
motivation: The author wanted structure to start from folders rather than notes, because a folder-organised collection loses its organising line in the graph view's single cloud.
problem: The graph view mixes every note into one cloud and ignores folders, so a collection organised by subject and chapter has no visible structure or a place to read alongside it.

relations.evidence: Once installed there is no path to configure — the plugin finds it on its own.

summary: Folder-based card map that draws link structure, reads PDFs and images beside it, and hides cards for recall.
